final_answer:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM
To: Patricia Huang, General Counsel, Greenfield Consumer Products Inc. | From: Aldridge & Whitmore LLP ESG Group | Re: Gap analysis of draft FY2024 ESG Report (3/10/2025), with remediation roadmap | Law stated as of the 4/7/2025 delivery date; Part 7 notes later developments verified through 10/2/2026.

1. BOTTOM LINE
Do not publish as drafted. Six items are Critical (securities-liability exposure) because they state present or historical facts that Greenfield's own records contradict: (1) net-zero "all scopes by 2040" versus the Board's Scope 1/2-only 2045 target; (2) Scope 3 total of 3,640,000 t versus the workbook's 3,840,000 t; (3) "100% of facilities assessed" versus 19/23 (82.6%); (4) "aligned with SBTi" while validation is pending; (5) Scope 3 "evaluated fifteen categories" while the workbook says no relevance screening was done; (6) Scope 2 reported market-based only, with unreconciled workbook arithmetic. Coordinate with Hargrave & Fenton (Part 5). The checklist also overstates several requirements (Part 2).

2. LEGAL FRAMEWORK AND CORRECTIONS TO THE CHECKLIST
- SEC. The rules are final, not "proposed" (Rel. 33-11275, Mar. 6, 2024; stayed by the SEC Apr. 4, 2024, Eighth Circuit). For large accelerated filers (LAFs), Items 1500-1507 of Reg. S-K and Reg. S-X Art. 14 apply to Forms 10-K and registration statements, not to a stand-alone ESG report. Checklist errors: Scope 1/2 is first required for FY2026 (not FY2025), with limited assurance FY2029 and reasonable FY2033; Scope 3 is not required; board climate-expertise and GHG-intensity disclosure were dropped; Scope 2 may use either method or both; scenario analysis is not mandated but, if used and a risk is material, Item 1502(f) requires disclosure of the parameters and assumptions. Treat the "as though reinstated" instruction as a benchmark only; the report is subject to Exchange Act §10(b)/Rule 10b-5 and Securities Act §17(a) regardless.
- California. SB 253 and SB 261 apply to a "reporting entity" doing business in California, so the $1.34B subsidiary figure is the wrong test. Parent consolidated revenue ($8.7B) likely qualifies at the parent level (SB 261: >$500M). SB 253's first Scope 1/2 report covers FY2025 data (due 2026 on a CARB-set date), not 2026 data due 2027; Scope 3 begins 2027; Scope 1/2 limited assurance from 2026, reasonable from 2030. SB 261 follows TCFD (or IFRS S2) and permits explanation of gaps; the checklist overstates it as mandating quantitative, temperature-specific analysis. Check AB 1305 (Cal. Health & Safety Code §44475 et seq.) for net-zero claims.
- EU. The checklist's €40M "large" threshold is outdated (now €50M turnover/€25M assets/250 employees). ESRS 1 lets first-year reporters omit comparatives, so FY2024 data is not a mandatory baseline; ESRS 2 GOV-1 requires expertise "or access to" it, not named directors; CSDDD likely does not reach Greenfield (EU turnover €780M is below the €1.5B non-EU test), contrary to the checklist.

3. FINDINGS (severity | requirement | evidence | remediation)
CRITICAL
C1 Net-zero misstatement. Draft (CEO letter; ESG Goals table; §4.1) claims net-zero across all scopes by 2040; Board Resolution (9/15/2024) §III.B adopts Scope 1/2-only net-zero by 2045, §IV.C declines any Scope 3 net-zero, §IV.E forbids implying otherwise, §V.C directs the GC to ensure accuracy. Draft §7.1 describes the Board action only as "affirm[ing] commitment to climate leadership." The 25% Scope 3 target is only "noted" as submitted to SBTi (§IV.B), not Board-adopted, yet the draft says "established." Requirements: Rule 10b-5; SEC Item 1504 (if filed); AB 1305; ESRS E1-1/E1-4. Remedy: conform to the resolution; describe the Scope 3 target as submitted and pending Board recommendation due Q2 2025; delete "most ambitious in our peer group" unless substantiated.
C2 Scope 3 figure and progress. Draft §§4.1, 5.2 report 3,640,000 t (-13.3%) and total 4,266,000 t; the workbook (Summary, Scope 3 Detail, Historical) and the draft's own category table sum to 3,840,000 t (-8.6%), total 4,466,000; the Goals table says 8.6%. The Compensation Committee minutes (8/8/2024) cite approximately 3.8M. Remedy: correct to 3,840,000/-8.6%/4,466,000 and the derived percentages (Scope 3 about 86.0%); investigate how the error arose (Apex).
C3 Vulnerability assessments. Draft §6.2: "100%" complete. Tracker (updated 3/5/2025, five days before the draft): 19/23; all 3 SE Asia sites in progress (HCMC, Bangkok, Hanoi), Gdańsk not started; $900M (22.8%) of $3,940M assets unassessed. Remedy: restate as 19 of 23 with revised dates, or complete first. Related: the $1.2B "high-risk" table includes two unassessed sites (HCMC $310M, Gdańsk $120M) and omits Houston ($210M, rated High); the tracker's $1.2B is a plug ("canonical risk zone mapping"). Completed High-rated assets total $980M. Rebuild the table with stated methodology.
C4 SBTi. Draft §4.1 says targets are "aligned with" SBTi and "consistent with" its criteria. SBTi emails (7/22/2024, 11/13/2024) say targets are not validated, that "aligned with" must not be used, and that validation is expected by Q2 2025. Remedy: use only "submitted to SBTi for validation"; disclose pending status and non-approval risk.
C5 Scope 3 completeness. Draft §5.1 says Greenfield "evaluated the fifteen Scope 3 categories" and reports "those most material." The workbook (Scope 3 Detail A18; Methodology) says no screening was conducted and 10 categories (including 2, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10) were "not assessed." Scope 3 ±20% uncertainty and data-quality scores of 2 for Categories 1 and 11 (about 73% of Scope 3) are undisclosed; methodology labels differ (Cat. 4 hybrid, Cat. 11 Apex proprietary modeling). SBTi has already flagged the screening gap. Requirements: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard; SB 253; ESRS E1-6. Remedy: delete the claim; complete documented 15-category screening before SBTi responds.
C6 Scope 2 and assurance presentation. (a) The draft reports only market-based Scope 2 (214,000). The workbook and Ridgeway report location-based 289,000 and say both "should be disclosed." Dual reporting is required by the GHG Protocol (hence SB 253 and ESRS E1-6); the SEC rule does not mandate it. Omission hides that RECs/GOs account for 75,000 t and location-based Scope 1+2 fell only 16.8% versus the 22.5% headline. (b) The workbook's facility detail sums to 341,695 (location) and 262,305 (market), not 289,000/214,000; the difference (52,695/48,305) is labeled "rounding reconciliation." (c) The workbook includes facilities (Jakarta, Rotterdam, Sacramento) that do not match the draft's facility list (no Indonesia, Netherlands or Hanoi plant in the workbook). Remedy: reconcile; confirm with Apex and Ridgeway that assurance covered corrected figures; present both methods.
HIGH
H1 Assurance description. Draft says emissions were "verified" and cites ISAE 3000 (Revised) and ISAE 3410; the letter cites ISAE 3410 and AICPA AT-C 210, and says "limited assurance," not verification. The draft's Appendix B is a summary and omits the location-based figure, although the letter permits reproduction only "in its entirety without modification... or summarization." The 2021 baseline and trend were not assured (first engagement), which the draft does not state. The letter, dated 2/28/2025, refers to a draft report dated 3/10/2025: query date. Ridgeway is also the financial auditor: confirm audit committee pre-approval (SEC Rule 2-01 of Reg. S-X). Remedy: reproduce the full letter; correct standards; disclose unassured baseline.
H2 Climate risk quantification (Okafor's concern is correct). §§6.2-6.3 give "moderate/severe" and "moderate/aggressive policy" scenarios, qualitative only, with no temperature pathways, time horizons, financial effects, capex or impairment estimates, though $340M (3.9%) of revenue sits in high-carbon solvents and EU ETS cost was €8.2M. Requirements: SEC Item 1502 and Reg. S-X 14-02 if filed; SB 261/TCFD; ESRS E1-9 (phase-in relief). Remedy: define horizons; model 1.5°C and high-warming pathways; quantify principal risks. Reconcile the €8.2M ETS cost with EU Scope 1 (workbook about 94,000 t).
H3 Governance and compensation. Draft §7.3 is silent on ESG metrics; minutes (8/8/2024) show the STIP is entirely financial, ESG metrics were considered, and the Committee deferred them to FY2025 (revised proposal due March 2025). Silence is misleading by omission when read against the draft's "alignment" language; ESRS 2 GOV-3 requires an express statement. No director climate competencies are identified (ESRS GOV-1; SEC no longer requires). Remedy: state no ESG metrics, the deferral and its status; add director competencies.
H4 Internal governance inconsistencies. The draft says the Sustainability Committee met 2/15, 5/9, 8/8, 11/14/2024 with full attendance; the resolution says its meetings were Oct 2023, Jan, Apr, Jul 2024; the Compensation Committee shows the same dates, yet its minutes put Okafor and Reinhardt at its 8/8 meeting and set its next meeting for 11/7. The draft gives the Compensation Committee four members (minutes: three) and the Board eight directors, 3 female (resolution: nine). Remedy: verify against corporate records. Also note the minutes describe Northbridge as "independent compensation consultant" while your email calls it a financial advisor: assess independence under Reg. S-K Item 407(e)(3)(iv) and NYSE 303A.05.
H5 EU readiness. No double materiality assessment (draft's assessment is stakeholder/financial; ESRS 1, IRO-1/2); no ESRS mapping; no E1-5 energy mix, E1-7, E2 pollutant data, E3-4 water consumption/discharge by water-stress area (only 18.4M m³ withdrawal, intensity -8%; confirm stress status of Marseille, Phoenix, Denver, Southeast Asia), E5-4/5-5 (no disposal breakdown: 62% diversion implies about 54,000 t disposed; "energy recovery" counted as diversion), S1 (contract types, pay gap, collective bargaining, contractor injuries; TRIR benchmark unsourced), S2 (Tier 1 only; 78% audit coverage), G1. The draft says 8,500 EU employees; your email says about 4,100: reconcile, since scope turns on headcount.
MEDIUM
M1 Add intensity metric (workbook: 72.0 t/$M, S1+2). M2 Disclose accurately that no internal carbon price is used. M3 Add GWP basis (AR5) and gas disaggregation. M4 Facility lists differ across draft, tracker and workbook (e.g., California, Ohio, Illinois, New Jersey in draft; none in tracker): reconcile; matters for SB 253 nexus. M5 Forward-looking boilerplate does not protect historical-fact errors (PSLRA §21E).
LOW
L1 GRI index "Partially Reported" entries. L2 CSDDD note. L3 Pre-dated "Published April 2025" legend.

4. INTERNAL CONSISTENCY SECTION (cross-reference summary)
Workbook: C2, C5, C6, M1, M4. Board resolution: C1, H4. Tracker: C3, M4. SBTi: C4, C5. Compensation minutes: H3, H4, Scope 3 approximately 3.8M. Ridgeway: C6, H1. Verified consistent: Scope 1 total (412,000), 17.3%, 31.0%, 22.5%, 626,000, $340M/3.9%, 34,200 employees.

5. SECURITIES-LAW IMPLICATIONS (C1-C6, H1)
Rule 10b-5 requires material misstatement, scienter and reliance; concrete statements of target scope, completion rates and validation status are verifiable facts rather than puffery. Scienter risk is aggravated because the tracker, workbook, SBTi emails and resolution predate the draft and are in company hands, the resolution directs accuracy,. Section 11 applies only if the report is incorporated into a registration statement (draft disclaims incorporation; verify shelf, S-8, hyperlinks). Comparable SEC ESG actions: SEC v. Vale S.A. (E.D.N.Y. 2022); Keurig Dr Pepper (2024). Caremark oversight exposure for directors. Hargrave & Fenton must align the 10-K and proxy with corrected figures, climate-risk factors, and compensation disclosure. Privilege: the Board resolution and minutes are corporate business records and probably not privileged in any dispute despite labeling; the General Counsel's overlapping roles (corporate secretary, designated accuracy reviewer, Mr. Vasquez's supervisor) argue for Audit/Sustainability Committee oversight of remediation.

6. REMEDIATION ROADMAP
P0 (before publication; target 4/14-4/21/2025): fix C1-C6, H1, H4 corrections with Board sign-off, Ridgeway re-confirmation and Hargrave review. Delay 4/30 publication if C3 or C6 stays open.
P1 (by 6/30/2025): Scope 3 screening; Board Scope 3 recommendation (Resolution §IV.D); SBTi response; quantified scenario analysis; compensation proposal; DMA kickoff.
P2 (by 1/1/2026 and FY2025 reporting): SB 261 TCFD report; SB 253 data controls and assurance; ESRS gap closure and Greenfield Europe GmbH data collection; supplier due diligence beyond Tier 1; water/waste/S1 data.
P3: reasonable-assurance readiness; Scope 3 primary data.

7. DEVELOPMENTS AFTER DELIVERY (verified)
SEC voted 3/27/2025 to end its defense; the Eighth Circuit held the case in abeyance in September 2025; the SEC proposed rescission in 2026, so treat the SEC regime as a benchmark only. Ninth Circuit enjoined SB 261 enforcement on 11/18/2025 but not SB 253 (CARB proposed 8/10/2026 for first reports). EU: Stop-the-Clock moved wave 2 to FY2027; Omnibus I (published 2/26/2026) limits CSRD to over 1,000 employees and €450M turnover and non-EU groups to over €450M EU turnover with an EU subsidiary or branch above €200M, from FY2028. Greenfield Europe GmbH likely remains in scope (headcount to be confirmed).
